bibliographic.title: Generative AI for pre-consultation mental health triage in disorders of gut-brain interaction
bibliographic.authors: Dakai Zeng, He Zeng, Jie Song, Kai Zhu
bibliographic.citation_apa: Zeng, D., Zeng, H., Song, J., & Zhu, K. (2026). Generative AI for pre-consultation mental health triage in disorders of gut-brain interaction. Frontiers in Psychiatry, 17, 1854670. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyt.2026.1854670

methodology.study_design: proposal of supervised pre-consultation triage model with governance conditions
methodology.technology_context: GenAI-enabled intake tool and conversational systems for pre-consultation mental health triage in gastroenterology/psychogastroenterology; LLM mentioned in safety safeguards for escalation-sensitive content

eligibility.decision_rationale: Peer-reviewed conceptual article proposing a constrained, auditable GenAI pre-consultation triage model for DGBI with explicit governance conditions (clinician review, escalation rules, safety/equity evaluation). Highly relevant to conversational governance in regulated healthcare, but not an empirical implementation or evaluation study.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Provided excerpts are partial (pages 1-2, 7-8); confirm article type, full governance framework sections, and absence of unreported empirical components.

appraisal.notes: Clear conceptual proposal aligned with its aim; strong governance framing but no empirical sample, dataset, or prospective evaluation reported in supplied text. Appraisal reflects conceptual/theoretical contribution only.

cerqual.explanation: Internally coherent governance-oriented framework for supervised GenAI triage in a regulated clinical setting, but supplied text lacks empirical findings or operational deployment evidence, limiting adequacy for outcome claims.

coding.theme: Governance conditions for constrained GenAI conversational triage
coding.subtheme: Human-in-the-loop pre-consultation mental health triage in DGBI
concepts: prospective evaluation across workflow safety equity acceptability
rq_alignment: human oversight and escalation in regulated healthcare
supervised triage rather than autonomous diagnosis

synthesis.main_claim: DGBI is a suitable setting for supervised GenAI-enabled pre-consultation triage that summarizes patient histories, screens distress, flags escalation, and routes care without replacing specialist judgment, provided five governance conditions are met.
synthesis.contribution: Articulates a practical, governance-centered design for constrained, auditable GenAI intake in regulated gastroenterology/mental health pathways, including rule-based bypass of generative synthesis for safety-critical disclosures and clinician-review workflows.
synthesis.limitations: Conceptual proposal without reported empirical implementation, sample, or prospective evaluation in the supplied text; manuscript preparation used GenAI only for language editing.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting conceptual evidence on governance design for LLM/GenAI conversational triage in healthcare: human oversight, escalation rules, auditable workflows, and safety-sensitive routing.

evidence.claim: Article proposes supervised GenAI pre-consultation triage rather than autonomous diagnosis.
Five governance conditions for acceptable systems are specified.
evidence.excerpt: five conditions are essential: a narrowly deﬁned triage task, multidomain but proportionate data collection, explicit rules for medical and psychiatric escalation, clinician review before action, and prospective evaluation

evidence.claim: GenAI tools should be constrained, auditable, and embedded in multidisciplinary care.
evidence.excerpt: useful precisely because they are constrained, auditable, and embedded in multidisciplinary care

evidence.claim: Mental health-related AI tools require clinician oversight and clear limits.
evidence.excerpt: mental health- related AI tools require clear limits, clinician oversight, and careful attention to context

evidence.claim: Safety-critical disclosures should bypass generative synthesis and use deterministic routing.
evidence.excerpt: escalation-sensitive content—suicidal ideation, self-harm, severe nutritional risk—should bypass the generative synthesis step entirely and follow deterministic, rule-based routing

evidence.claim: LLM paraphrases of safety-critical disclosures introduce unacceptable risk.
evidence.excerpt: LLM- generated paraphrases of safety-critical disclosures introduce unac- ceptable risk

evidence.claim: Safeguards aim to make hallucination visible and correctable within clinician-review workflow.
evidence.excerpt: These safeguards make hallucination visible and correctable within the clinician-review workﬂow

evidence.claim: Prospective evaluation should cover workflow, safety, equity, and patient acceptability.
evidence.excerpt: prospective evaluation across workﬂow, safety, equity, and patient acceptability

evidence.claim: Peer-reviewed publication in Frontiers in Psychiatry.
Authors used GenAI only for manuscript language editing, not for data or conclusions.
evidence.excerpt: generative AI was used in the prepara- tion of this manuscript solely for language editing and polishing
